issue: Lambda function shares an IAM execution role with another function
fix: Create a unique IAM execution role for this Lambda function instead of sharing role GetAtt:StartIngestionJobFunctionRole with . Lambda functions should have a 1:1 relationship with IAM execution roles.
suppressionReason: Accepted (scanner false positive): StartIngestionJobFunctionRole is referenced exactly once in this template (StartIngestionJobFunction, Role: !GetAtt "StartIngestionJobFunctionRole.Arn") and by nothing else - grep confirms a single consumer, and every Lambda in nested/bedrockkb/template.yaml has its own distinct role (S3VectorManagerRole, OpenSearchLambdaExecutionRole, StartIngestionJobFunctionRole). The check's own generated fix text names no second function ("...sharing role GetAtt:StartIngestionJobFunctionRole with ." - blank), i.e. the scanner found no actual sharer. The 1:1 function-to-role relationship the check asks for already holds. Disposition changed resolved -> suppressed because 'resolved' is not sticky: SRT re-detects the finding on every scan and reopens it.

issue: This .npmrc does not set a minimum release age or sets it too low. Newly published packages can be malicious or unstable. Add `min-release-age = 7` to wait 7 days before resolving newly published package versions. Added in: v11.10 Reference: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-18-npm-bulk-trusted-publishing-config-and-script-security-now-generally-available/
suppressionReason: Accepted — the mitigation is in the tree but not yet effective. src/ui/.npmrc DOES set min-release-age=7 (added in the SRT/ASH remediation), so the rule's ask is satisfied in-tree. It is inert in CI for now: the key requires npm >= 11.10, while .gitlab-ci.yml pins npm@11.1.0 and src/ui/package.json engines still allow npm >= 10, so today it only emits an 'Unknown user config' warning. It costs nothing meanwhile (npm ci installs from the committed lockfile and resolves nothing from the registry) and starts protecting the `npm install` path as soon as the build npm reaches 11.10. Kept as 'suppressed' rather than 'resolved' because 'resolved' is not sticky: semgrep keys on (path, line, issue) and this rule's message text changes, so each rule-text update would re-open the finding — and run.py now blocks 'reopened' as well as 'open', which would fail CI on an unrelated rule edit.

issue: Ensure WAF prevents message lookup in Log4j2. See CVE-2021-44228 aka log4jshell
fix: Add a rule to your AWS::WAFv2::WebACL resource that blocks requests containing Log4j2 JNDI lookup patterns. Create a ByteMatchSet with pattern strings like '${jndi:' and configure your WAF to block these patterns. This protects against Log4Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-44228) that could allow remote code execution.
suppressionReason: Accepted: WebACL uses DefaultAction Block with an explicit IP allowlist (deny-by-default), so the Log4j managed rule group adds no protection for already-blocked traffic.

issue: API Gateway lacks proper authentication configuration (AuthorizationType is NONE)
fix: Set AuthorizationType to 'AWS_IAM', 'COGNITO_USER_POOLS', or 'CUSTOM' and configure appropriate authorization settings.
suppressionReason: Accepted: intentional public static-asset route (enabled only when ServeWebUI=true). This GET serves the React SPA shell (index.html) from S3 to the browser BEFORE the user authenticates in-app; auth happens later against the Cognito-authorized /op POST. A JWT cannot be attached to the browser's initial document fetch, so AuthorizationType NONE is required, and only non-sensitive static UI files are exposed. Defense-in-depth: the stage-level WAFv2 IP allowlist (IsWafEnabled) and the PRIVATE-endpoint VPC policy (UsePrivateApi) still gate this route.

issue: API Gateway does not have access logging enabled with proper retention
fix: Ensure both DestinationArn and Format properties are specified in AccessLogSetting
suppressionReason: Accepted (scanner limitation): the stage DOES configure AccessLogSetting with both a DestinationArn (HttpApiAccessLogGroup, KMS-encrypted, RetentionInDays=LogRetentionDays) and a JSON Format, but they are wrapped in Fn::If [EnableApiAccessLogs] (on at LogLevel INFO/DEBUG). SRT's security-matrix cannot resolve Fn::If, so it does not see the DestinationArn/Format inside the conditional branch. Access logging is correctly implemented; the conditionality is intentional to avoid log costs at higher LogLevels.

issue: API Gateway does not have CloudWatch logs enabled
fix: Enable CloudWatch logs by setting MethodSettings with LoggingLevel to INFO or ERROR.
suppressionReason: Accepted (scanner limitation): the stage DOES set MethodSettings with LoggingLevel ERROR for ResourcePath '/*' HttpMethod '*', but wrapped in Fn::If [EnableApiAccessLogs]. SRT cannot resolve Fn::If and reads MethodSettings as a non-array, so it reports execution logging disabled. Execution logging is deliberately ERROR-only (INFO would echo full request/response payloads, incl. customer document data, into CloudWatch); JSON access logs cover request metadata. Logging is correctly implemented; the conditionality is intentional.

issue: DynamoDB data plane events are not captured by CloudTrail logging
fix:
Enable CloudTrail logging for DynamoDB data plane events for this table. Create a CloudTrail Trail if none exists. Add this table's ARN to an EventSelector with DataResources type 'AWS::DynamoDB::Table' — append to existing values array if one exists, otherwise create a new EventSelector. For CDK: use the L1 escape hatch (trail.node.defaultChild as CfnTrail).eventSelectors as DataResourceType.DYNAMODB_TABLE does not exist.

IMPORTANT - S3 Bucket Logging Requirements:
If creating a new S3 bucket for CloudTrail logs:
1. First check if the template already has an S3 bucket configured as a logging destination (look for buckets referenced in other buckets' LoggingConfiguration.DestinationBucketName)
2. If a logging bucket exists, configure the new CloudTrail bucket's LoggingConfiguration to use it with LoggingPrefix 'cloudtrail-logs/'
3. If no logging bucket exists, create a dedicated server access logging bucket first, then configure the CloudTrail bucket to log to it with LoggingPrefix 'cloudtrail-logs/'
suppressionReason: Accepted: CloudTrail DynamoDB data-plane logging is an account-level control (trail + log bucket) owned by the deploying customer; the solution template cannot assume or create account-wide trails. Consistent with all other DynamoDB tables in this solution.

issue: Lambda function IAM role violates principle of least privilege
fix: Replace wildcard actions (e.g., '*' or 'service:*') with specific actions that the Lambda function actually needs, and restrict resources to specific ARNs instead of using '*'.
suppressionReason: Partially accepted: the bedrock-agentcore:* action wildcard was removed — the role now grants only the five runtime APIs the handler calls. Two of them, CreateAgentRuntime and ListAgentRuntimes, declare no resource type in the IAM service authorization reference, so they remain on Resource '*'; Get/Update/DeleteAgentRuntime are scoped to this account/region's runtime/* ARNs (the runtime id is service-generated, so the id segment stays a wildcard). iam:PassRole/CreateServiceLinkedRole and logs are scoped.

issue: KMS key deployed without monitoring infrastructure for events and compliance
fix: Add EventBridge rule with EventPattern source "aws.kms" and Lambda function target for KMS event monitoring. The Lambda function should have X-Ray tracing enabled. The Lambda function should have CloudWatch Alarms for the following Lambda metrics: Errors, Throttles, Duration, Invocations, ConcurrentExecutions, and DeadLetterErrors.
suppressionReason: Accepted: KMS key event monitoring (EventBridge rule + monitoring Lambda + alarms) is account-level infrastructure owned by the account operator, out of scope for this template. Same rationale as the other KMS-007 records in this baseline. This service is deployed by an extension SELLER into their own Marketplace seller account, so KMS-event monitoring is theirs to configure against their existing CloudTrail. The service's own security-relevant events are already recorded independently: the API access log records every caller account, the activation roster records every attempt, and a CloudWatch metric filter alarms on refusals.

issue: Lambda function may contain sensitive data in environment variables
fix: Use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store for sensitive environment variables like 'CLIENT_SECRET'. Replace direct values with references like '{{resolve:secretsmanager:MySecret:SecretString:password}}' or use dynamic references with Ref or GetAtt.
suppressionReason: Accepted (test fixture, not product infrastructure): scripts/security/live_checks/oidc_provider/ is a throwaway OIDC identity provider that only exists to verify the Cognito pre-token IdP group-mapping trigger (see .claude/skills/live-auth-checks.md). It is deployed by a manual `make verify-idp-federation` run and deleted immediately after; it is not referenced by template.yaml or any nested stack, and never runs in a customer account. The flagged environment variables are the fixture's RSA private exponent and OIDC client secret. Both are generated per run by deploy.py (rsa_parameters / secrets.token_urlsafe), sign nothing but this fixture's own test tokens, and are destroyed with the stack. There is no real credential to protect.

fix: Create CloudWatch alarms for the following Lambda metrics: Errors,Throttles,Duration,Invocations,ConcurrentExecutions,DeadLetterErrors. Configure alarm actions (e.g., SNS notifications) to assign an owner who will monitor and respond to incidents.
suppressionReason: Accepted (test fixture, not product infrastructure): scripts/security/live_checks/oidc_provider/ is a throwaway OIDC identity provider that only exists to verify the Cognito pre-token IdP group-mapping trigger (see .claude/skills/live-auth-checks.md). It is deployed by a manual `make verify-idp-federation` run and deleted immediately after; it is not referenced by template.yaml or any nested stack, and never runs in a customer account. CloudWatch alarms presuppose an on-call owner and a lifetime longer than one verification run. A failure here fails the verification script, which is the intended signal.

issue: API Gateway has 2 method(s) without request validation
fix: Create a RequestValidator resource AFTER the RestApi definition (it references the API, so the API must exist first). Then update EACH Method resource to include a reference to the validator.
suppressionReason: Accepted (test fixture, not product infrastructure): scripts/security/live_checks/oidc_provider/ is a throwaway OIDC identity provider that only exists to verify the Cognito pre-token IdP group-mapping trigger (see .claude/skills/live-auth-checks.md). It is deployed by a manual `make verify-idp-federation` run and deleted immediately after; it is not referenced by template.yaml or any nested stack, and never runs in a customer account. INHERENT to the protocol: an OIDC provider must accept the arbitrary query and form parameters that /authorize and /token carry (redirect_uri, state, scope, code, grant_type, client_id, client_secret...). Attaching a RequestValidator would reject valid OIDC requests and break the flow this fixture exists to exercise.
